grid.$description: Layout primitive for arranging children in a CSS grid — display:grid + a curated gap scale, nothing else. Column count/sizing isn't tokenized: unlike gap (a real spacing-scale concept), a column count is a per-use structural decision (2 vs. 3 vs. 6 columns depends entirely on the content), not something that benefits from a fixed design-token scale — same reasoning Box applied to not tokenizing radius. No surface/border/padding of its own — Grid only arranges children; wrap it in a Box if the grid area itself needs a background/border. Gap steps deliberately mirror Box's padding scale exactly (same none/xs/sm/md/lg names, same dim aliases) since both are 'a slot from the spacing scale' — reusing one naming/value set instead of inventing a second.

xs.$description: 8px — the base gap, per dim's own legend.

md.$description: 16px — 'comfortable padding — card/input padding' per dim's own legend.

lg.$description: 24px — gap between distinct components, per dim's own legend.
